title: Canonical small-etale restriction and comparisons on algebraic-space tests
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal C\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ be a category fibred in groupoids, with based functors, discrete algebraic-space tests and two-isomorphisms as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Its fppf topology, regular-function ring sheaf and module sheaves are those of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra] and [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For algebraic spaces and their small etale sites [def-trf-algebraic-space], use the canonical ambient module operations of [def-sfb-space-ambient-module-operations] on the chart categories of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A test $z:V\to\mathcal C$ gives the functor from $V_{et}$ to $\mathcal C$ obtained by including scheme charts then applying $z$; it is continuous for the fppf topology. The based-functor equality identifies the underlying chart schemes. Pullback of regular functions along this canonical scheme isomorphism, in the fixed ULift coordinates, is natural on charts and gives the ring map defining module restriction $H_z$ by actual precomposition on section carriers and restrictions. For $a:V\to W$ and $\theta:z\Rightarrow t a$, on every compatible pair of scheme charts $(T\to V,T\to U)$ the defining arrow is $\theta_T$ followed by $t(T\to U)$. There exists a unique natural transformation $c_{a,\theta}:a^*H_t\to H_z$ sending every local tensor $b\otimes s$ to $b$ times restriction of $s$ along this arrow; define the comparison to be this unique transformation. Define the tensor identity by its unique normalization $b\otimes s\mapsto b\,s|_T$, and the tensor compositor by its unique normalization $c\otimes(d\otimes s)\mapsto c\,a^\sharp(d)\otimes s$, using the actual composite chart of [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition]. For schemes regarded as algebraic spaces [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space], the map attached to a scheme arrow is its Yoneda map. On every small etale slice, additive sheafification exists in any universe containing the site-object universe and inverts exactly locally bijective maps. These universal properties fix the constructions independently of the comparison-calculus theorem.
